activity_c.text: Good morning, everyone.
Today I am going to explain a common and important process that you regularly practise in the ICT laboratory.
This process is setting up and testing a basic computer network.
Although it is a standard task, it must be carried out in a clear and logical sequence, because mistakes during setup can cause connection problems later and affect system performance.
First, you have to check the network diagram carefully, because it shows how devices must be connected.
Before handling any equipment, the overall layout should be clearly understood.
Then, you have to identify the correct ports on the switch and router so that cables are placed properly.
After that, you have to prepare the network cables to ensure reliable data transmission.
Next, you have to label the cables clearly to reduce confusion during troubleshooting.
You shouldn’t power on the devices at this stage, because all physical connections must be completed first.
Proper preparation helps minimise configuration errors.
Once preparation is complete, you have to connect computers to the switch using the correct Ethernet cables.
Then, you have to connect the router to the switch, because the router controls network access.
After that, you have to connect the server or main workstation so that shared resources can be accessed.
Cable connections should be checked carefully to ensure they are firm and secure.
You don’t have to configure software settings yet, because hardware connections must be verified first.
Correct physical connections support stable network communication.
Finally, you have to power on the network devices in the correct order to allow proper startup.
Then, you have to test network connectivity using basic commands to confirm communication between devices.
After that, you have to check indicator lights on the switch and router to identify connection status.
Any faults should be reported clearly so that corrective action can be taken.
You shouldn’t install advanced network services at this stage, because the session focuses only on setup and testing.
Following this sequence ensures a reliable, stable, and functional network.
